sheets.name: battle-part-panel-labels
sheets.notes: Row captions of the BATTLE parts panel - the overlay the d-pad cycles through a Medabot's parts while a robottle is running. Row 3 reads '<action caption> <action name>' and row 4 either 'AP <cost>' or '<uses caption> n/ n'. 30 tiles, one pointer at 0x654BBC, no twin. The captions are NOT text and NOT glyph-bank cells: they are pre-rendered 4bpp pixels, body 15 over an index-5 rim, decompressed into the EWRAM tile pool at 0x02002474 and DMA'd tile by tile into BG0 by the loop at 0x0801C880. That is why the kanji codes (E003 E00B for the action caption, E014 E018 for the uses one) turn up only inside ordinary sentences, why repainting those codes in either glyph bank changes nothing on these rows, and why blanking their glyphs in the kanji font at 0x6593D0 changes nothing either. The sheet is a DEDUPLICATED atlas addressed by a tilemap the panel builds in RAM, so nothing lines up in a 4-wide view and every label is a tile RUN: with tiles_wide=4 a height-1 rect [x,y,w,1] simply names tiles y*4+x .. +w-1. Runs used: action caption tiles 0-2 over 4-6 (one 3x2 rect, because those happen to be a clean rectangle), uses caption tiles 7-9 over 10-12 (two height-1 runs with the top 4 / -4 split that 'battle-action-names' uses, since 7-9 and 10-12 are not 4 apart). Tile 3 is the shared blank - never draw on it; the panel puts it in the column between a caption and its value, which is why the uses row has 8px of clearance and the action row has none. top=4 puts the 9px capitals on the same band as the value beside them. Both rects are 24px, so a label must measure <=22: draw() does not add the rim to measure() and a 24px word loses its outline on both edges. 'Ac.' is 16px and lands on exactly the kanji's own x=4..19, keeping the original 6px gap before the action name ('Acc.' is 22px and closes that gap to 3, which reads as 'Acc.Tir'; 'Accion' needs 35). 'Uso' is 18px ('Usos' is 24, two over the limit). The other label groups in this block - a second AP plate and a TYPE plate - are already Latin; nothing else here is Japanese.
sheets.verified: gbashot from work/battle-panel.state on the es build: right,right -> frame 120 shows 'Ac. Tir'; right,down,right,down,left,up -> frame 400 shows 'Uso 3/ 3'

sheets.name: battle-start-banner
sheets.notes: Whole block is one 80x16 banner (20 tiles, 10 wide, 2 rows) reading 'combat start'. The single label covers the entire sheet. Original ink: fill 15 / outline 5 over transparent index 0, glyphs on pixel rows 2-13; top:4 puts the 8px-tall Latin line plus its outline on rows 3-12, i.e. centred. The sheet is only half the story: the box on screen is painted by a twelve-cell tilemap that pads its corners with the sheet's blank tile and makes the banner's top-row columns 3 and 4 share one tile, which shredded the first letters of any Latin word. navi/gfx.py (BATTLE_BANNER_MAP) straightens that map to ten one-to-one columns and pads the corners with the banner's own outer columns instead, so the text must measure 62px or less for those columns to stay blank — the build checks them and leaves the Japanese banner untouched if they carry ink. 'Robobatalla' (the GLOSSARY canon) is 61px; the tight-UI fallbacks are '¡BATALLA!' (58px) and 'Batalla'. Recompresses to 304B against 270B in ROM, so the block relocates; it has exactly one pointer site, 0x654BC4, which pointer_index() finds automatically, so the repoint is covered.

sheets.name: part-slot-banners
sheets.notes: Deduplicated tileset (44 unique tiles, no repeats) arranged by an LZ77 tilemap that sits uncompressed-adjacent right after each block: 0x648DE8 for 0x648B44 and 0x6FD5D8 for 0x6FD334 (the two maps are byte-identical too). The map is 8x8 entries = four 8x2-tile banners stacked: head / right arm / left arm / legs, each = 2 icon tiles + 6 caption tiles. Do NOT touch the maps; they are not patched by this spec. Because tiles_wide=8 is the SHEET stride and not the screen stride, every tile_rect here is height 1 and simply names a linear run of tiles: [x,y,w,1] = tiles y*8+x .. y*8+x+w-1. Runs used: head caption top 0x02-0x06 and bottom 0x0A-0x0E; shared arm caption top 0x11-0x14; shared caption tail 0x15-0x16 and 0x1A-0x1D (blanked); right-arm private bottom 0x18-0x19; left-arm private bottom 0x21-0x22; legs caption top 0x23-0x26 and bottom 0x29-0x2B. Icon tiles (0x00,0x01,0x08,0x09,0x0F,0x10,0x17,0x1E,0x1F,0x20,0x27,0x28) and the shared blank tile 0x07 are left alone - the icons are the Medabot silhouette with the relevant limb lit, and they carry the head/r-arm/l-arm/legs distinction. Hard constraint from the dedup: the two arm banners share every caption tile except a 16x8 box (tiles 0x18-0x19 vs 0x21-0x22), so they cannot carry different words. Solution used: both read 'Brazo' on the upper 8px line and the private box carries 'd.' / 'i.' on the lower line; the lit icon plus the marker identify the slot. Captions are 8px capitals+lowercase from the dialogue font (the Japanese was a 12px drawn face spanning both tile rows), so each label is one 8px line at top=0; the second tile row of head and legs is cleared with a ' ' label. Fits measured: Cabeza 36px in 40, Brazo 30px in 32, Patas 29px in 32, d. 8px and i. 6px in 16. Recompresses to 572B against the original 676B, so it lands in place at both write sites; no relocation, no repoint.

sheets.name: part-compare-head-banner
sheets.notes: Not 'the remaining slot banners' the backlog guessed: this is the whole part-COMPARE screen (41 unique tiles) and its 30x20 tilemap is the LZ77 block right after it at 0x6FD8D8. Rendered through that map the screen is two side-by-side part panels, each headed by the same banner as sheet part-slot-banners' first row, plus two vertical 'HEAD' gauges, two selector triangles and the window frame. The only Japanese pixels in the block are the one head caption; the other three slot banners live in 0x6FD334/0x648B44 and the game swaps them in. Tiles 0x03-0x09 are the banner's top row and 0x0A-0x10 its bottom row (0x03,0x04,0x0A,0x0B = icon), each used twice by the map, one instance per panel, so a single redraw fixes both panels. tile_rect is height 1 and names a linear tile run: [x,y,w,1] = tiles y*8+x ..; caption top = 0x05-0x09, caption bottom = 0x0C-0x10 (cleared). The banner tiles are byte-identical to 0x648B44's tiles 0x02-0x06 / 0x0A-0x0E, so 'Cabeza' is drawn in the same 40px box at the same 8px line and the two screens match pixel for pixel. Everything else is untouched: 'HEAD', the arrows and the frame are Latin/art and stay. Do not patch the tilemap. Recompresses to 608B against the original 620B - in place, no relocation.

sheets.name: battle-action-names
sheets.notes: Ten 32x16 action-type plates (naguru / utsu / gamushara / neraiuchi / mamoru / setchi / naosu / tokushu / ouen / bougai) built from a DEDUPLICATED 69-tile sheet arranged by an LZ77 tilemap at 0x6469F4 (160B = 80 entries = 10 boxes of 4x2, plain indices 0x00-0x44, no flip/palette bits). Only one copy of that map exists in the ROM; 0x660C64 is a byte-identical second copy of the tile sheet and takes the same bytes. Do NOT patch the map - every rect below is a linear tile run on the sheet's own stride 4, so [x,y,w,1] = tiles y*4+x onward and [x,y,w,2] = that run plus the run 4 tiles later. Box -> tiles (top row / bottom row): 0 naguru 00,01,02,03 / 04,05,06,07 | 1 utsu 08,09,0A,03 / 0B,0C,0D,03 | 2 gamushara 0E-11 / 12-15 | 3 neraiuchi 16-19 / 1A-1D | 4 mamoru 1E,1F,20,03 / 21,22,23,07 | 5 setchi 24,0A,25,03 / 26,27,28,03 | 6 naosu 00,29,2A,2B / 04,2C,2D,03 | 7 tokushu 2E-31 / 32-35 | 8 ouen 29,36,37,38 / 39-3C | 9 bougai 3D-40 / 41-44. FIVE tiles are shared between boxes and force the whole design: 0x03 is the blank filler used by boxes 0,1,4,5,6 (never written - it is the only untouched tile left); 0x00+0x04 are column 0 of BOTH naguru and naosu (the two words both began with the kana na); 0x29 is naosu's column 1 top AND ouen's column 0 top (both began with o); 0x07 is naguru's and mamoru's column 3 bottom; 0x0A is utsu's column 2 top AND setchi's column 1 top. Consequences: (a) naguru and naosu can never show different pixels in column 0, so 0x00/0x04 are blanked and both words live in columns 1-2 = 16px - 'Gol' (golpe) and 'Ar.' (arregla); (b) naosu must use 0x29, so its first 8px double as ouen's first 8px - both words are made to start with the same 7px capital A at x0 ('Ar.' is 16px in a 16px box, 'Apoyo' is 31px in a 32px box, so both land at x0), which makes the shared tile correct for both and lets Apoyo keep its full width; ouen is therefore drawn as two labels, 'poyo' (23px, columns 1-3 top, lands at x8) over the full 'Apoyo' (bottom row), the A's top half coming from the repair label; (c) 0x07 is turned into a shared period at local x1-2 so both 'Gol.' and 'Def.' read as abbreviations - mamoru is padded to ' Def' so its f ends 2px before it; (d) setchi's TOP row (0x24,0x0A,0x25) is not contiguous on the sheet, so no run can carry proportional text across it: setchi and utsu are both typeset one character per tile (monospaced 8px pitch, six labels each), which also makes the shared 0x0A hold the same glyph 'r' in both - 'Tir' (tiro) and 'Tra' (trampa). The three-tile boxes that ARE contiguous (mamoru, naosu) use two 1-row runs with top:4 / top:-4, which splits the 9-row glyph at row 4; the four fully private boxes (gamushara, neraiuchi, tokushu, bougai) use one 4x2 rect at top:4. Ink sampled from the original: fill 15 white, outline 5 mid grey, glyph band rows 3-13, so top:4 reproduces it. Wording: nothing here was English in the original, everything was kana. 'Frena' matches the bougai/妨害 button already redrawn in status-buttons-a.json. Verified: 26 labels drawn, 0 skipped, every tile the map references is either written or the deliberate blank 0x03, and the block recompresses to 700B against 823B, so it is written in place at BOTH 0x6466BC and 0x660C64 - no relocation, no repoint.

sheets.name: menu-status-labels
sheets.notes: Companion of navi-ui-labels (0x7ED058): the same menu, drawn DARK ON A LIGHT PLATE instead of white on transparent. 380 deduplicated tiles; an UNCOMPRESSED 16x40 BG map follows the block at 0x7F32D0 (pointed at from 0x7C9F4 and 0x7CD10) - decode it first, the sheet is unreadable linearly. Do NOT patch the map: tiles_wide 16 is the SHEET stride and every tile_rect is a linear tile run, y*16+x onward; because map rows 0-3 are tiles 0x01-0x40 in order, the two-tile-tall menu buttons happen to be vertically adjacent at that stride, which is why menu.allies uses h=2. PALETTE: index 0 is transparent (outside the plate), 1 is the ink and the plate's top rule, 7/8 the bevel shading, 9 the face of the highlighted button state, 4 the face of the dimmed state, 2/3 the bevel line under the rule. apply_sheet_labels clears a rect to index 0, which on this sheet would punch a transparent hole through the plate, so each label is drawn in four passes that exploit two properties of Typesetter._outline: (a) when fill == outline the outline pass floods every zero pixel that is reachable rightwards/downwards from the glyph ink, so a wide 'I' run paints the whole rect one solid colour, and its `top` chooses the first row the flood reaches (top 6 leaves rows 0-4 untouched at zero, top 0 fills everything); (b) the '…' glyph inks only its bottom row, so '…' at top -7/-5/-3 lays a single continuous 1px rule on row 0/2/4, each rule bleeding exactly one row upward into the still-zero row above it. Painting bottom-up - face (top 6), bevel row 4, shade row 2, rule row 0 - rebuilds the button chrome as 1,8,8,2,2 against the original 1,7,8,1,2: rows 1 and 3 land one palette step off, invisible on hardware, everything else is pixel-identical. The filler strings must stay as generated: the 'I' run has to be wide enough that it starts at x<=1 or the flood never reaches the left edge, and the '…' run is padded with SPACES only - '·' or any other pad inks rows the rule pass must leave alone. Then the Spanish is drawn with keep_background over the finished plate, fill 1 (outline 1 is a no-op once no zero pixels remain). Widths: Grupo 30px and Ficha 28px in 32px boxes. 仲間配置's button is one h=2 rect; ステータス's two tile rows are 13 apart in the sheet, not 16, so it is split into a chrome-only top rect and a text rect on the bottom row - both words end up on rows 8-15 of their button, so the menu stays aligned. SKIPPED, and why: (1) メダロッチ (rows 0-1) and メダロット生産 (rows 4-5) share tiles 0x01,0x02/0x11,0x12 (state A) and 0x05,0x06/0x15,0x16 (state B) - the first 16px of both words - and their private tails are only 16px and 24px wide. Both stay Japanese, which in turn pins tiles 0x03 and 0x07: those are also cells of セーブ's top row, so セーブ cannot be repainted either without notching メダロッチ's bevel. (2) The 8px katakana labels in map rows 12-15 and the plate headers in rows 24-39 draw from one shared glyph pool: ブロック is 0xA4-0xA7 (32px, and 'Bloque' measures 34px), メンバー is 0xA8-0xAB but only three of its four tiles appear in the ブロックメンバー and TEAM-plate instances, and チームメンバー is assembled as 0xB4-0xBA in row 14 and as 0xB4,0xB5,0xB3,0xA8,0xA9,0xAA in row 38 - the same tiles at different offsets, so one redraw cannot satisfy every instance. (3) メダロットセレクト (0xBB-0xC2) and フィールドセレクト (0x178-0x17B + 0xBF-0xC2) share their last four tiles, the セレクト tail; blanking the tail leaves 32px heads, and neither 'Medabot' (42px) nor a descender-safe verb fits - 'Elegir' loses the g's tail in an 8px row. Both are translated on 0x7ED058 instead, where the same two labels have 56px and 48px of private run. (4) English stays English: PAGE, TYPE, LEVEL, TEAM, MEDAROT, MEDAROTER, LEADER, ROBOTTLE!, MEDALINK, the navi logo, both digit sets. Vocabulary is shared with navi-ui-labels: 仲間配置 -> Grupo, ステータス -> Ficha (Estado is 35px and does not fit the 32px buttons; one term is used on both sheets so the menus agree). Recompresses to 4269B against 4415B in ROM, so it lands in place; if a later edit grows it, the block has exactly one pointer, 0x7CC8C, which pointer_index() finds, so relocation is covered.

sheets.name: navi-ui-labels
sheets.notes: Navi/out-of-battle UI label atlas: 320 deduplicated tiles, white (15) ink with a mid-grey (5) outline over transparent index 0 - the same ink pair as part-slot-banners, so a plain clear+draw works and no background trickery is needed. TILEMAP: an UNCOMPRESSED 16x28 BG map sits immediately after the block, at 0x7EDEC6 (448 u16 entries, tile index in bits 0-9, h/v flip in bits 10-11). Decode it before touching anything: rendered linearly the sheet looks like noise, because the artwork is a 128x224 label sheet that was deduplicated tile by tile. Do NOT patch the map; every rect below is a linear tile run - tiles_wide 16 is the SHEET stride, so [x,y,w,1] names tiles y*16+x .. y*16+x+w-1, and the run may cross the 16-tile boundary. Runs used (tile hex): allies 0x1A-0x1B blanked + 0x1C-0x20 text + 0x27-0x2C blanked; items 0x47-0x4B text + 0x50-0x55 blanked; status 0x5A-0x60 blanked + 0x68-0x6E text; save 0x72-0x75 text + 0x79-0x7C blanked; medabot-select 0x97-0x9D text + 0x9E blanked; field-select 0xF1-0xF7 text; HUD status 0x10B-0x10F text. Two of those runs reach outside their own label and are deliberate: 0x9E is the shared final ト of both セレクト headers, so blanking it serves the medabot header and the field header at once, and 0x5D inside the status top run is the upper half of the ー in パーツ on map row 15 - it holds nothing but one row of outline pixels, so blanking it thins that bar by 1px and nothing else. A tile-level diff of the patched block touches only map rows 2, 3, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 14, 15, 21 and 23, i.e. exactly the labels listed here. Every menu word was a 16px-tall drawn face spanning two tile rows whose halves are NOT adjacent in the sheet, so each label is one 8px Latin line on whichever of the two rows is a clean private run, and the other row is cleared with a ' ' label. Widths measured: Grupo 30/40, Bolsa 28/40, Ficha 28/56 and 28/40, Salva 28/32, Medabot 42/56, Campo 30/56. The dialogue font is 9 rows tall in an 8px rect, so the descender row is clipped: p and j survive that (Grupo, Campo read fine) but g does not - 'Elegir' rendered as 'Eleair', which is why the two select headers took nouns instead. SKIPPED, and why: (1) メダロッチ (rows 0-1) and メダロット生産 (rows 4-5) share tiles 0x01,0x02,0x04,0x05 on the top row and 0x0E-0x12 on the bottom, i.e. the first 40px of both words is the same pixels; no pair of Spanish words can share a 40px prefix and still say 'Medawatch' and 'build a Medabot', and blanking the shared head would leave each label a 16px private tail. Both stay Japanese. (2) The 8x8 katakana strip in map rows 12-15 (ブロックメンバー / メンバーリスト / ブロックデータ / チームメンバー / メダル / パーツ / 仲間 / ロボトル) is a shared pseudo-font: tile 0x86 (メ) is cell 4 of one label, cell 0 of another and cell 3 of a third, 0x89 (ー) and 0x8B (バ) likewise, and 0x82-0x85 (ブロック) is the prefix of two different words. The same 8px slice would have to read as three different letters, so nothing there can be redrawn; the widest private run left over is 24-32px, below 'Bloque' (34px) anyway. (3) 時間 is 2 tiles (16px) and its second tile 0xA5 is shared with the 間 of 仲間; 進行度 is 3 tiles (24px). Both too narrow for Spanish. (4) English stays English per the glossary: PAGE, MEDAROT, MEDAROTER, TYPE, LEVEL, TEAM, LEADER, ROBOTTLE!, the navi logo and both digit sets are untouched. One cosmetic compromise: 仲間配置's tile 0x1B appears again v-flipped on the label's bottom row, so it is blanked and the word starts two cells in - 'Grupo' sits 16px right of where the Japanese started. INTEGRATION - READ FIRST: this block has NO pointer anywhere in the ROM (pointer_index finds nothing for 0x7ED058, nor for its map at 0x7EDEC6; the nearest lead is 0x0782C -> 0x7ED000, a byte table that ends 0x58 before the 'Le' header, and 0x7E6A0/0x7E6F8/0x7E770/0x7E7D4/0x7E8E0 -> 0x7EDEC8, i.e. map entry 1). patch_sheets would report 'grew, and nothing points at it' if the block grew, so this spec is sized to land IN PLACE: it recompresses to 3485B against 3694B in ROM. Keep it that way, or find the loader before shipping.

sheets.name: parts-medal-status
sheets.notes: Mixed Latin/Japanese sheet, 96 tiles, no tilemap of its own in the neighbourhood (the next compressed block 0x663188 is more tile data, not a map; the 0x663E0C-0x664100 raw maps belong to other tilesets), so the label groups were recovered from pixel continuity instead. The sheet is a deduplicated pool of 16px-tall plates stored as a top-tile run followed, at a per-label distance, by its bottom-tile run: PARTS 0x00-0x06 / 0x17-0x1D, MEDAL 0x09-0x0D / 0x1E-0x22, MEDACHANGE 0x0E-0x16 / 0x24-0x2C, /TYPE 0x2D-0x31 / 0x32-0x36, then the two kanji plates, then small 8px Latin plates (MF, No.1/No.2/No.3, a couple of two-letter bits) at 0x43-0x56 and nine gauge-bar tiles at 0x57-0x5F. Tile 0x07 is the shared blank. Everything Latin STAYS: PARTS, MEDAL, MEDACHANGE (the transformation, an English franchise word the game itself writes in Latin - the backlog's 'ADVANCE / MEDICAL' was two misreads of this one word), TYPE, MF and the No.n plates are untouched. The only Japanese pixels are two 24x16 plates on the medal panel: 属性 (attribute) = top tiles 0x37-0x39 over bottom tiles 0x3D-0x3F, and 性格 (personality/character) = top 0x3A-0x3C over bottom 0x40-0x42. Their bottom run sits exactly 6 tiles after their top run, which is why tiles_wide is 6: at that stride [1,9,3,2] names 0x37,0x38,0x39 over 0x3D,0x3E,0x3F and [4,9,3,2] names 0x3A,0x3B,0x3C over 0x40,0x41,0x42 (the rect walks the stride, so x=4 w=3 correctly runs past the row edge into 0x3C/0x42). tiles_wide is a spec-local stride only and no other label uses it. Ink sampled from the kanji: fill 15 (white), outline 5 (dark blue in this screen's palette), background index 0 - the same values as the PARTS plate, so the two redrawn plates match the Latin ones. The original kanji ink spans rows 0-14 of the plate while PARTS spans rows 2-12; top=3 puts the 9px Latin line plus its outline on rows 2-12, i.e. exactly the PARTS band. Each plate is 24px wide, which is the hard limit: 'Tipo' measures 23px and 'Alma' 23px, so both centre with the outline column clipped on one side only, exactly like ROBOBATALLA in battle-start-banner. Rejected for width: 'Clase' 28px, 'Modo' 25px (one pixel over - the literal choice for 性格 and the first thing to try if the plate ever gets a fourth tile), 'Genio' 28px, 'Perfil' 32px, 'Índole' 31px. 'Alma' was chosen over the abbreviations because the Medal IS the Medabot's soul in franchise terms and this field is the medal's temperament, shown right under 'Tipo' on the same panel. The two labels touch exactly 12 tiles (0x37-0x42) and nothing else - verified by diffing the patched tile array against the original. Recompresses to 984B against 978B in ROM, so the block relocates; it has exactly one pointer site, 0x654BD4, which pointer_index() finds, so the repoint is covered.

sheets.name: parts-status-tileset
sheets.notes:
The parts/medal status tileset: 188 deduplicated tiles arranged by the LZ77 tilemap that sits in the next compressed block, 0x6FC9D8 (14460B decompressed = 7230 BG entries, 30x20 = 600 per screen, twelve screens plus a 30-entry tail). Do NOT patch the map; this spec is tile runs only. Screens 0-3 are the MEDAL pages, 4-7 the head / right-arm / left-arm / leg part pages, 8-11 the same four parts in list view (same captions, different value grid). Every tile is referenced, none is spare. tiles_wide=8 is the SHEET stride, not a screen stride: every tile_rect is height 1 and simply names a linear run, [x,y,w,1] = tiles y*8+x .. y*8+x+w-1 (runs may cross the nominal row edge, e.g. [7,19,3,1] = 159,160,161).

WHAT STAYS. Latin already on screen is untouched: LV (5,6,8,9), EXP inside the medal box, MF and AP (73,74,77,78 / 141,142,144,145), the MF 1 / MF 2 / MF 3 headers (54,55,56/61/70), the digits 1 2 3 (44,48,51,52,53), the rotated side tabs MEDAL / HEAD / R-ARM / L-ARM / LEG (10-14, 102-105, 136-143, 151,152, 162,165,168), the Medabot slot icons (88,89,95,96,121,122,129,146-148,157,158), the gauge cells (49,50), the marker icons (83,185) and every window-frame tile (0-4,7,15-21). 72 tiles left alone, 116 redrawn.

GEOMETRY. The Japanese was a condensed 8x16 face: each stat label is two kanji side by side inside a 16x16 box (2x2 tiles), so the Spanish gets two stacked 8px lines of two capitals = a four-letter abbreviation. Ink is fill 6 with outline 5, the exact values the kanji used (6 = stroke, 5 = the rim around it, 0 = transparent); the slot captions are fill 15 / outline 5 like the original yellow-on-black banner text. Capitals occupy all 8 rows, so top:0 on both lines and the pair fills the box edge to edge, the way the two kanji did.

THE THREE DEDUP TRAPS (why three labels are shorter than the rest):
1. Tile 31 is the top half of the 性 in BOTH 属性 (screens 1,4,5,6,7) and 相性 (screen 1). Two labels cannot put different pixels in one tile, so tile 31 is blanked for both and each word keeps only its private bottom row: 属性 -> TP (tipo), 相性 -> AF (afinidad). Their private top-left cells (30, 38) are blanked too.
2. Tile 138 is a one-pixel-different variant of tile 33 used only by screen 5 (right arm), so the right-arm 属性 box reads 30,31/32,138 instead of 30,31/32,33. Fix: draw 'TP' into the 16px rect [32,33] and 'P' alone into the 8px rect [138]. That reproduces tile 33 byte-for-byte because the widths line up - 'TP' is T(7)+1+P(6)=13 in 16px, so it starts at x1, T ends at x7 and P sits at x9-14, exactly where an 8px canvas centres a 6-wide P (start 1). Verified: tiles 33 and 138 are byte-identical after the patch. Any replacement text must keep that property (first letter 6 or 7 wide, second letter 6 or 7 wide, at least one of them 7, or the two tiles drift and the right-arm screen shows a broken glyph).
3. Tile 69 is the bottom half of the 功 in BOTH 成功 (screens 4,5,6) and 必要成功 (screen 3). Blanked for both. 成功 therefore keeps only its top row and reads PR (precisión); 必要成功 gets its full top row (62-65) for 'PREC.' and only three of its four bottom tiles (66,67,68) for 'REQ.', which happens to align nicely - both lines start at x2.
Non-traps: tiles 71,72,75,76 (消費) are shared by 消費MF and 消費AP, and 41,42,43,45,46,47 (熟練度) by all three 熟練度N rows - same word each time, so one pair of labels serves them all.

SLOT CAPTIONS. Same dedup shape as part-slot-banners.json, and the same wording so the two sheets agree. Right and left arm share their whole caption top row (123-128) and the tail of the bottom row (132-135); the legs share 127,128 and 133,134,135 with them. So: 'Brazo' goes on the shared top run 123-126 and the two private bottom boxes carry 'd.' (130,131) and 'i.' (149,150); 'Patas' goes on the legs' private top run 153-156 and its private bottom run 159-161 is cleared; every shared tail tile is blanked. Head is private end to end: 'Cabeza' on 90-94, 97-101 cleared. The lit-limb silhouette icon is what distinguishes the four anyway, exactly as in the sibling sheet.

WORD LIST (Japanese -> Spanish, all measured to fit): 属性 TP, 性格 PE/RS (personalidad), 相性 AF, 熟練度 PERI/CIA, 残りEXP -> EXP / REST (28px in 32; EXP kept, redrawn 8px tall so the two lines fit), 行動 AC/TO, 必要成功 PREC./REQ., 消費 CO/ST (reads COST MF and COST AP with the untouched MF/AP), 対象 OB/JE (objetivo), 射程 AL/CA (alcance), 装甲 BL/IN (blindaje - armadura is out because ARMA reads as weapon), 回数 US/OS, 成功 PR, 威力 DA/ÑO, 推進 PR/OP, 機動 MO/VI (movilidad), 防御 DE/FE, 近接 CU/ER (cuerpo a cuerpo), 遠隔 DI/ST (a distancia). CUER and DIST are the melee/ranged pair on the leg page and must stay distinct from BLIN and DEFE, which share that page.

FITS. Cabeza 36/40, Brazo 30/32, Patas 29/32, d. 8/16, i. 6/16, PERI 24/24 (flush, as the three kanji were), CIA 18/24, PREC. 30/32, REQ. 23/24, EXP 21/32, REST 28/32, the two-capital lines 10-14px in 16. Nothing is skipped by the typesetter.

SIZE. Recompresses to 2028B against 2277B in ROM, so it lands in place at 0x6FC0F0 - no relocation, no repoint, and the tilemap block right behind it is not disturbed.

sheets.name: status-tab-bar
sheets.notes: 26 tiles arranged by an LZ77 tilemap in the next compressed block, 0x648894 (108B = 54 entries, 6 wide x 9 rows = a 48x72 window). Do NOT patch the map. Rows: 0 = header rule (tiles 0,1,1,1,1,2); 1 = [3][4][5][6][7][3 H-flipped] = のうりょく; 2/4/6 = [3][8][8][8][8][3^H] spacers; 3 = [3][9..13] = メダフォース; 5 = [3][14..18] = じゅくれんど; 7 = [3][19..23] = ローテーション; 8 = [24 = the ▶ cursor][25 blank x5]. tiles_wide is 1 here, so every tile_rect is [0, first_tile, run_length, 1] and simply names a linear run. KEY FACT: this window is NOT transparent - the body is palette index 4, the ink is index 1 with an index-3 drop shadow, and index 0 appears only in tile 25 (below the window), i.e. index 0 IS the transparent backdrop. A plain label would clear() the rect to 0 and punch see-through holes in the panel, so each row is repainted with a WASH first: one label with fill=4/outline=4 (clears to 0, stamps 'HHHH' in 4, and the outline pass dilates the 4-region by 1px) followed by three more identical labels with keep_background, each dilating another pixel until the whole strip is solid body colour again; only then is the caption drawn with keep_background, fill=1, outline=3 (the outline pass paints nothing because no zero pixels are left, which matches the original - the Japanese had a soft shadow, not a ring). Verified: after the patch every pixel of tiles 4-23 is 1, 3 or 4, never 0. SECOND TRAP: rows 3/5/7 have no separate right-border tile - the window's 1px right edge (index 1 at column 7) is baked into tiles 13, 18 and 23 along with the last kana. Washing those tiles would leave the panel with a dashed right edge, so they are cleaned with keep_background stamps instead: drawing '▲:'/'¡' (tile 13), '▲:'/':▲'/'D' (tile 18) and '▲'/'↓' (tile 23) in fill=4 covers exactly the kana ink of each tile and never touches column 7 (the stamp sets were found by set-cover over the font's glyph shapes). The captions then run over the full 40px (tiles 9-13 / 14-18 / 19-23) with keep_background so the restored border survives; each caption is short enough that its ink stops at column 38 at the latest. Row 1 is only 32px (tiles 4-7) because its right border is a separate H-flipped copy of the shared border tile 3, which must not be touched. Trailing spaces on three captions pull them flush left, matching the Japanese, which was left-aligned at x=8 rather than centred: 'Aptit.' 30px, 'Medaf. ' 38px, 'Destr.  ' 40px, 'Rotac.  ' 40px, all inside their rects. All four words are abbreviations with a full stop because nothing longer fits: Aptitud 39px and Medafuerza 61px overflow 32/40px, Destreza is 47px and Rotación 45px. Recompresses to 332B against 462B in ROM, so it lands in place; the single pointer site is 0x6462F4 if it ever needs to move.

sheets.name: effect-word-plates
sheets.notes: 23 tiles = two 48x16 plates, white (15) text with an index-5 outline inside a rounded white frame, all over transparent 0. No tilemap is adjacent (the next block, 0x661D18, is a different graphic). Layout recovered from the frame corners and edge continuity: plate 1 (シフト) = top tiles 0-5 over bottom tiles 6-11, a clean 6-wide linear pair, so tiles_wide 6 makes rows 0 and 1 of the spec match the screen exactly. Plate 2 (パワー) = top tiles 12-17 over bottom tiles 18,19,20,**9**,21,22 - only eleven tiles are private to it because the sheet is deduplicated: tile 9 is the bottom of フ in plate 1 AND the bottom of ワ in plate 2, at the same plate column (x=24..31). Two consequences drive the whole spec. (1) Plate 2's bottom row is NOT a contiguous sheet run, so it cannot carry text at all - a rect over tiles 18-22 would scramble on screen because tile 9 sits between 20 and 21. (2) Anything written into tile 9 shows up in both plates. Both captions therefore live in the plate's TOP tile row only (rects [0,0,6,1] and [0,2,6,1], 48px, top 0) and both bottom rows are blanked - plate 1's blank covers tiles 6-11 including the shared tile 9, and plate 2's blank covers 18-22, so the shared tile ends up empty for both. Sibling context: the neighbouring block 0x661568 holds the same family of effect labels already drawn in Latin (TRAP, PLANT, CLEAR, RESCUE, CROSS, OUT), and str:0930C5 shows シフト sitting in the part-effect list next to いりょく/ぼうぎょ/せっち/かいふく/かいじょ/へんか/ぼうがい, so these two are effect-category names: シフト = CAMBIO, パワー = PODER (PODER rather than FUERZA to keep it distinct from Medafuerza). Uppercase matches the Latin siblings; CAMBIO is 40px and PODER 34px inside 48px. KNOWN COST, flagged deliberately: the rounded white frame cannot be kept. Every tile of the plate carries a piece of it (top border on rows 0-2 of the upper tiles, bottom border on rows 5-7 of the lower tiles, side borders in the end tiles), the frame is never separable at tile granularity, and the typesetter can only clear a rect to 0 or paint non-zero pixels - there is no way to erase the kana without erasing the frame, and no way to repaint transparent. The result is a frameless white-with-outline caption, which is exactly the style the neighbouring part-type plates (0x661958) already use, but it is a visible restyle: if that is not acceptable, drop this sheet rather than half-doing it. Captions also sit in the upper 8px of the 16px plate instead of centred, because the lower half cannot be written. Recompresses to 280B against 330B in ROM, so it lands in place; the single pointer site is 0x654B88.

sheets.name: corrupt-save-message
sheets.notes: The corrupted-save error plate: 84 tiles = 168x32, stored in plain screen order at stride 21 (4 tile rows), no dedup and no tilemap involved, so the sheet reads left to right exactly as it is drawn and a rect patch is safe. Two 16px text bands, one sentence each: 'the saved data is broken' over 'please play from the beginning'. The original glyphs are a 12px face, 12 per band on the first line and 14 on the second (the second line runs the full 168px, x 0-166), inked on pixel rows 0-10 and 16-26; the bottom 5 rows of the plate are blank. The block uses ONLY palette values 0 and 15 - there is no outline colour anywhere in it - so both labels set outline:0, which makes Typesetter._outline a no-op and keeps the flat white-on-transparent look; the pipeline default of 5 would add a grey rim the plate never had. top:1 centres the 9px Latin line inside the 11px the Japanese ink used, so the redraw lands on rows 1-9 and 17-25 and the line spacing is pixel-identical to the original. Each label's rect covers a whole band ([0,0,21,2] and [0,2,21,2]), so the clear wipes every Japanese pixel including the tall marks, and apply_sheet_labels centres the text: line 1 measures 151px and line 2 140px inside 168px (margins 8/9 and 14/14, nothing clipped). Wording is tuteo like the game's own 'Guarda tu progreso', no final period (the original has no punctuation); the longer literal 'Los datos guardados se dañaron' is 171px and would be refused. Recompresses to 493B against the original 546B, so it writes in place at 0x6428CC - no relocation, no repoint. Verified: the block has no byte-identical twin elsewhere in the ROM (unlike the slot-banner and action-name sheets) and exactly one pointer site, 0xC3C4, which pointer_index() would find if a longer wording ever pushed it over 546B.

sheets.name: attack-stamp-slash-a
sheets.notes: Left half of the two-part attack stamp that reads 一閃 ('a single flash', the slash/flash a big hit throws up). 16 tiles = one 32x32 OBJ (4x4, 1-D mapping), and the sheet is the whole sprite, so tiles_wide 4 makes the spec grid the screen grid. This half holds only 一: a tapered brush bar on pixel rows 11-18, spanning almost the full 32px, vertically centred in the cell - i.e. the left character of a 64x32 two-character word whose right half is block 0x6EA72C (閃). Ink is INVERTED against the rest of the pack: body = index 8 (a mid tone), outline = index 15 (white), over transparent 0, with a handful of 9/10/11 pixels for the brush shading; fill 8 / outline 15 reproduces it. Split at a WORD boundary on purpose: each half is a whole Spanish word, so the stamp still reads whether the game lays the two sprites out side by side ('¡UN TAJO!') or stacked, and a seam gap only ever looks like a wide word space. '¡UN' is 16px inside 32px. Recompresses to 144B against the 144B original, so it is written IN PLACE, no relocation; its single pointer site is 0x6E59A4 (entry 65 of the battle-effect graphics table that starts at 0x6E58A0), which pointer_index() finds on its own. KNOWN COST: the original is a 32px-tall brush kanji and the dialogue font is 9px, so the stamp goes from a poster-sized glyph to a small caption inside the same box. There is no bigger font to draw with; the alternative is leaving Japanese on screen every time the effect fires.

sheets.name: attack-stamp-slash-b
sheets.notes: Right half of the 一閃 stamp: 16 tiles = one 32x32 OBJ (4x4, 1-D mapping) holding the single character 閃 (門 with 人 inside), drawn edge to edge on rows 1-30. Pairs with 0x6EA69C (一) to its left. Same inverted ink as the left half: body index 8, outline index 15, transparent 0. 'TAJO!' measures exactly 32px in a 32px cell, so it is flush: the text is complete but the 1px outline column is clipped off the left of the T and the right of the !. If that reads badly over a busy battle scene the drop-in fallback is 'TAJO' (29px) with 'UN' (13px) in the left half, losing the exclamation but gaining a margin on both sides; 'RAYO!' (32px) or '¡ZAS!' (28px, then the left half becomes blank) are the other two candidates if the effect turns out to be a beam rather than a blade - 一閃 is 'one flash' and reads as a sword flash in most games, which is why TAJO was picked. Recompresses to 180B against the 266B original, so it is written IN PLACE; single pointer site 0x6E59A8 (entry 66 of the graphics table at 0x6E58A0), found automatically. Same KNOWN COST as the left half: 32px brush kanji becomes 9px Latin text.

sheets.name: attack-stamp-fixed-a
sheets.notes: Left half of the second two-part stamp, which reads 一定 ('fixed / constant / for certain'). 16 tiles = one 32x32 OBJ (4x4, 1-D mapping); this half holds only 一, a tapered brush bar on pixel rows 12-21 spanning the full 32px, and the right half is block 0x6F130C (定). Its bar is drawn slightly differently from the 一 of 一閃 (0x6EA69C), which is the evidence that the two bars are the first character of two separate words rather than one reused decoration. Same inverted ink as the other stamp: body index 8, outline index 15, transparent 0. '¡DE' is 16px inside 32px. Recompresses to 140B against the 137B original - 3B over, so this is the ONE block of the four that relocates; single pointer site 0x6E5B58 (entry 174 of the graphics table at 0x6E58A0), found automatically by pointer_index(). TRANSLATION IS A JUDGEMENT CALL, flagged: the transcription 一定 is certain (the glyph is 宀 over 疋, element for element), but its trigger was never reproduced - 40000 frames from work/jp-bat.state with A mashed never loads these tiles into VRAM, and the neighbours in the graphics table are single icons (star, crosshair, cannon, heart, LV plate) rather than one animation's frames, so the mechanic behind it is unconfirmed. '¡DE FIJO!' takes 一定 in its everyday sense, 'for sure, without fail', which fits any of the plausible mechanics (guaranteed hit, fixed damage, locked aim) without inventing one. Drop-in alternatives, same rects/fill/outline/top: '¡ES' + 'FIJO!' (plainer), 'TIRO' + 'FIJO' (if it turns out to be a shot), 'MIRA' + 'FIJA' (if it is a lock-on), 'DAÑO' + 'FIJO' (if it is fixed damage). Verify against a real trigger before shipping.

sheets.name: attack-stamp-fixed-b
sheets.notes: Right half of the 一定 stamp: 16 tiles = one 32x32 OBJ (4x4, 1-D mapping) holding the single character 定 (宀 over 疋), drawn edge to edge on rows 0-31. Pairs with 0x6F1280 (一) to its left. Body index 8, outline index 15, transparent 0, plus a few 9/10 pixels of brush shading that the clear removes. 'FIJO!' is 27px inside 32px, so unlike the 一閃 half it keeps a margin on both sides. Recompresses to 176B against the 306B original, so it is written IN PLACE; single pointer site 0x6E5B5C (entry 175 of the graphics table at 0x6E58A0). The word is split at a WORD boundary on purpose: each sprite carries a whole Spanish word, so '¡DE FIJO!' still reads whether the game places the two halves side by side or stacked, and the seam only ever shows as a wide word space (the two labels are centred inside their own cells, so the gap is 10px here). See attack-stamp-fixed-a for why the wording is a judgement call and for the drop-in alternatives. Same KNOWN COST as the other stamp: a 32px-tall brush kanji becomes a 9px Latin caption in the same box, because the dialogue font is the only font the build can draw with.

sheets.name: menu-status-labels-2
sheets.notes: Second pass over 0x7F2190, on top of menu-status-labels: the small-kana word pool and the SAVE button, which the first pass left in Japanese. MERGE BEFORE SHIPPING: patch_sheets snapshots `data = bytes(rom.data)` once, before its loop, so two sheet entries naming the same block do NOT compose - the second one decompresses the pristine block and its write clobbers the first (verified: with both entries in the list, menu-status-labels' tile 0x21 comes out unpatched). These labels must be appended to menu-status-labels' own `labels` array (no rect and no key collides; merged it draws 68 labels, touches 68 tiles and recompresses to 4202B against 4415B, so it still lands in place). PALETTE: the Medawatch screen draws this sheet on BG0 with palette bank 15 (work/medawatch.vram.bin), not a grey ramp: 1 = near-black green (the ink), 4 = light green and 9 = green (the two button faces), 8 = pink (the label plates), 7 = RED (the 1px highlight under every plate's black rule). SAVE BUTTON: on screen the bar is [icon][メダロッチ 4 tiles + 18 fill tiles][cap][セーブ 3 tiles][cap], so the save label has exactly 24px - 'Salva' (28px, what navi-ui-labels uses) does not fit and 'Guardar' is 42px; 'Save' measures 24px exactly and is the one word that fills the box. Its three chrome tiles are not contiguous in the sheet (0x70, 0x03, 0x71 for the light state, 0x72, 0x07, 0x73 for the dimmed one), so each is its own 8px chrome rect; the text row is contiguous (0x7B-0x7D and 0x7E-0x80). Tiles 0x03/0x07 are SHARED with メダロッチ, which stays Japanese: repainting them costs that label 2 ink pixels and gives its third cell the same 1,8,8,2,2 chrome the first pass already gives Grupo and Ficha (row 1 red -> pink, row 3 near-black -> dark green). Leaving them alone is worse: the red hairline then breaks into red/pink/red across the save button and two stray pixels float over the word. With palette 15 an exact 1,7,8,1,2 chrome is impossible here: each '…' pass paints its ink row plus the row above in one colour, so five different rows cannot be rebuilt; a dithered attempt (fill 7 and fill 1 passes over a painted row) renders as a chequerboard and is worse. THE 5-PIXEL BAND: the small-kana labels are NOT 8px tall. Each label tile is row 0 = 1 (rule), row 1 = 7 (red), rows 2-7 = 8 (plate); the kana are a 5px font living in rows 3-7, and the plate's remaining 3 inner rows are in the SHARED border tiles (0x91 x53) one map row below, which cannot be touched. The Latin font is 9 rows, so the text is drawn at top 0 and hangs from the plate's rule: x-height letters land exactly where the kana were and capitals/ascenders merge into the rule, which is index 1 like the ink, so it reads as a heading attached to the top line. The plate is rebuilt as row 0 = 1 and rows 1-7 = 8, i.e. the red highlight is lost over the words (the alternatives - a doubled black rule, or a dotted black/red rule - look worse; rendered all three with palette 15). RUNS AND SHARING (every tile of a word appears in the same order in every instance, so one redraw serves them all): ブロック 0xA4-0xA7 32px at strip 12/13 and plate 24; メンバー 0xA8-0xAA 24px at strip 12/13 and plates 22, 26, 38; リスト 0xAB-0xAD 24px at strip 13 and plate 26; データ 0xB0-0xB2 24px at strip 13 and plate 24; チー 0xB4-0xB5 16px at strip 14 and plates 28, 38; ムステータス 0xB6-0xBA 40px at strip 14 and plate 28. 0xB3 (the ム variant used before メ) is already blank. Widths force the vocabulary: 'Bloque' is 34px in a 32px run so it is abbreviated 'Bloq.' (25px); メンバー has 24px, which is four characters, hence 'Bots' (23px); リスト also has 24px and 'Lista' is 27px, so it is blanked and メンバーリスト reads 'Bots'; データ takes 'Info' (21px) because 'Datos' is 29px; ステータス keeps the pack's 'Ficha' (28px in 40px). チー is blanked because 'Team' is 25px in a 16px run, so チームステータス reads 'Ficha' and チームメンバー 'Bots'. 配置, the 16px kanji heading that sits outside the メンバー plate, is two non-adjacent tile pairs (0x124-0x125 over 0x12E-0x12F, both private) with a flat index-4 background; 16px fits no Spanish word, so both halves are erased and the plate reads 'Bots' alone instead of '配置Bots'. STILL JAPANESE, and why: メダロッチ and メダロット生産 share their first 16px (0x01,0x02 / 0x11,0x12 light, 0x05,0x06 / 0x15,0x16 dimmed) and メダロット生産's own text row is split between 0x11,0x12 and 0x4B-0x4D, so neither can be written without the other reading as its first two letters; メダロットセレクト and フィールドセレクト share the セレクト tail 0xBF-0xC2 and 'Medabot' is 42px in a 32px head (both are translated on 0x7ED058 instead); the 16px-tall row of メダル/パーツ/仲間/ロボトル/時間/進行度 is 16-32px per word AND its two tile rows are 14-15 apart in the sheet, not 16, so no rect spans them; the 8px kanji counter next to PAGE (0xA1,0xA2 over 0xAE,0xAF) is one cell wide. English stays English: PAGE, TYPE, LEVEL, TEAM, MEDAROT, MEDAROTER, LEADER, MEDALINK, ROBOTTLE!, the navi logo and the digit rows are untouched. || THE BAR TITLE (メダロッチ) - CHECKED, AND IT CANNOT BE WRITTEN. The wide green field is not a text field: the Medawatch bar is a CAROUSEL and that field holds whichever entry is selected, with its neighbours in the small plates beside it (pressing right swaps メダロッチ and セーブ between the two - captured with gbashot from work/es-corr.state, B opens the bar). That is what the two 'states' in this sheet are: face 4 = the wide selected field, face 9 = the small side plate, and every carousel entry is drawn in both. On screen (work/medawatch.vram.bin, BG0 map row 0) the title is [badge 0x75,0x76,0x87][0x05,0x06,0x07,0x08][0x60 x18][arrow 0x29][セーブ]: only FOUR tiles carry the title, 32px, and the 18 cells of green after it are eighteen copies of the single fill tile 0x60, so they add no width - anything drawn there would repeat eighteen times. 'Medarreloj' is 58px, so even the whole field could not hold it; 'Reloj' is 27px and would fit. What blocks it is sharing: メダロッチ and メダロット生産 both start with メダ, deduplicated to ONE pair of tiles per state - 0x01,0x02 over 0x11,0x12 (side plate) and 0x05,0x06 over 0x15,0x16 (wide field). So the first 16px of the title is also the first 16px of メダロット生産, which is another carousel entry (it is simply not unlocked yet in the save used for capture). Drawing 'Reloj' there renders メダロット生産 as 'Relット生産' - rendered it to be sure, work/shots/wf2_hypo_seisan.png. The private runs are 16px for the title (0x17,0x18) and 24px for メダロット生産 (0x4E,0x4F,0x50), and both labels centre inside their own rect, so the only way to write the title is a Spanish PAIR sharing a pixel-identical 16px head. A 16px head holds two letters ('Me' is 13px, 'Med' is 19px), and no Spanish word for 'produce Medabots' starts with the two letters of any Spanish word for 'Medawatch': the tails that fit 메ダロット生産's 24px are 'jora' (Mejora, wrong meaning), 'ear' (Crear, but no watch word starts with Cr) and 'ntar' (Montar, same problem), while 'dabot' needs 28px. Blanking the shared head instead leaves the title 16px, which fits no word ('Rel' and lowercase 'bot' are exactly 16px, 'Bot' is 17px, 'Hora' 24px). So the title stays Japanese: a wrong or half-Japanese label is worse than an untranslated one. That was true until the carousel was re-cut: medawatch-carousel now writes 'Medarreloj' over eight cells and メダロット生産 keeps its own tiles, so the parked labels this note used to describe are gone. The clean fix is out of reach of this tool: the block would have to grow by two tiles holding a private Spanish head, and the carousel's composition table - which is code, not the sheet's own map at 0x7F32D0 (the screen row mixes tiles from sheet rows 0, 2, 6 and 8, so the game does not copy that map) - would have to point the title at them. || SELECT PLATES (adjudicating a second sweep's reading of tiles 187-194): those are 0xBB-0xC2, and they are TWO runs, not one - メダロット is 0xBB-0xBE (32px, private to the メダロットセレクト plate on sheet row 30 and to strip row 14) and セレクト is 0xBF-0xC2 (32px), which also draws the tail of フィールドセレクト on sheet row 36. So the 64px 'Elegir Medabot' the sweep suggested would write half of itself into the field-select plate; 'Medabots' (47px) does not fit the 32px private head either. Handled the way 0x7ED058 handles the same pair: the shared tail is blanked and each private head carries the noun - 'Bots' (23px) and 'Campo' (30px, the term that sheet already uses for フィールド). The two plates then read 'Bots' and 'Campo'. || SAVE PANEL - MEASURED ON THE REAL SCREEN AND REJECTED. Captured it with gbashot (es-corr.state, B opens the bar, right selects セーブ, A opens the panel; VRAM in work/sv-panel.vram.bin) and read BG0's map. The sweep's tile numbers are right and its top:4 / top:-4 trick is right too - two rects, one per tile row, do rebuild a 16px-tall line, and that is how a 16px label would have to be drawn here. The blocker is horizontal. Each label owns only the tiles its kana cover, and every gap between a label and its number is the panel's global filler tile 0x62 (dozens of uses), so none of the slack is writable: 時間 has 16px (Tiempo 35, Hora 24, Time 23), メダル 24px (Medallas 45, Medalla 39, Medal 29), パーツ 24px and only on its lower row - its upper row is 0xC6, 0x62 (the shared filler, because the ー has no top half), 0xC7 - (Partes 35), 仲間 16px (Amigos 35), 進行度 24px (Avance 37). The one label with room, 勝ち／ロボトル数 at 0xCA-0xD0 over 0xD9-0xDF, is 64px but its seventh cell is 0xC5/0xD3 - the ル shared with メダル - so a 48px word (Ganadas 42, Batallas 43) would still leave a kana standing in the middle of it, and freeing that tile means blanking メダル, which has nothing that fits to put back. Nothing here was written.

sheets.name: medawatch-face
sheets.notes: The Medawatch's own face (BG2 of work/sw-hex.bin): three hexagonal buttons labelled メダロット / メダル / パーツ beside the Medabot figure. 492 tiles, one pointer at 0x7C6B8, so it relocates cleanly if it grows. Palette bank 1: ink is index 1 (near-black), the LIT hexagon's face is 4 (bright green) and the dimmed one's is 9 (teal), with 3 and 2 as the kana's own antialias - the redraw is flat, ink on face, and drops that antialias. EVERY BUTTON EXISTS TWICE, once per state, as a straight palette swap (4/3 <-> 9/2), so each label is two rects: メダロット 0x37-0x3A lit and 0xCD-0xD0 dimmed, メダル 0xEF-0xF1 and 0x70-0x72, パーツ 0x14D-0x150 and 0xAF-0xB2. Each run is linearly contiguous, and one run crosses a 16-tile row boundary, which _RectCanvas handles. The text band is a full 8px tile row here (unlike the 5px band of the 0x7F2190 plates), so the words sit exactly where the kana sat, drawn at top 0. WIDTHS ARE THE WHOLE STORY. The hexagon's interior is ~34px per button, but the tiles that make its slanted left and right edges are shared with the tile row below (same hexagon), so writing into them would repeat the letter 8px lower: the writable run is 32px for メダロット and パーツ, and 24px for メダル. None of the canon terms fit - Medabot is 42px, Medalla 39px, Partes 35px, and even Medal is 29px against メダル's 24px. So the buttons take the shortest unambiguous forms that do fit, read as a set of three: 'Bot' (17px, the clipping of Medabot - the panel is about the one Medabot shown beside it, so singular), 'Med.' (22px, Medalla; unambiguous next to 'Bot', which already carries the Medabot sense) and 'Parte' (29px; 'Partes' is 35px). Any of the three can be swapped for another string of the same width without touching the rects. 'Med.' is the weakest of the three and the first thing to revisit if the button ever gains a tile. THE KANA ARE ~10px TALL and spill into the neighbouring tile row - two rows above the line for メダロット and パーツ, one below it for メダル - so each label also carries a wipe rect for that row, or the redraw leaves dirt over the Spanish (rendered it first without them to be sure). Those neighbours are 0x2A-0x2C and 0xC9-0xCB (メダロット, lit/dim), 0xFB-0xFD and 0x81-0x83 (メダル), 0x48 and 0x8E + 0xA8 (パーツ). 0x8E is shared with the メダル hexagon's inside, where the wipe costs one pixel; everything else is private. The lit パーツ has no twin of 0xA8 anywhere in the block, so its upper row carries at most the single pixel of 0x48. In each label the text is drawn only on the main row, 8px at top 0, which puts it 2px below where the kana started - centred enough inside a hexagon that is 5 tile rows tall. ONE BLEMISH, kept on purpose: メダロット is the longest label and the tip of its メ reaches into the hexagon's slanted left-edge tile (0x36 lit, 0xCC dimmed), which is 5 columns of black outside, one of antialias and two of face. Flooding that tile is the only way the label machinery could erase those four pixels, and it turns the slope into a 5px bulge on the widest row of the hexagon - rendered both, work/shots/wf2_face_es.png against wf2_face_slope.png, and the bulge is far more visible. So four pixels of the old メ stay in the left edge of the Medabot button, clear of the word itself.

sheets.name: medawatch-carousel
sheets.notes: The Medawatch bar, re-cut. One entry per unlocked function, each drawn twice (small side plate, wide selected field) out of rectangles of the sheet's own tilemap at 0x7F32D0; navi/gfx.py documents the blitter (0x0807CC9C, taking cell, width and height), the composer (0x0807CD18), the entry list built at 0x0808009C and the two layout tables. 仲間配置 (Grupo) and ステータス (Ficha) keep their own cells and live in menu-status-labels. THE SHEET CANNOT GAIN A SINGLE TILE. It is decompressed straight into VRAM at 0x06004000 (0x0807CC42), so its 12160 bytes ARE the video memory and anything past them lands on the next graphic - a build that grew it to 421 tiles shipped once and turned the intro's station street into noise. So this sheet appends nothing: it only re-points cells (map_points) at tiles the sheet already has, and the tiles it frees pay for the ones it needs. THE CHROME IS THE GAME'S OWN, NOT A COPY. Every chrome row here is pointed at 0x5F (side plate) or 0x60 (wide field), the pure-chrome tiles the game already uses to pad the selected entry: rows 1,7,8,1,2 and 1,7,8,1,3 over the plate face, untouched. Painting a chrome tile instead was the first attempt and it shifted the frame's colours - the four-pass recipe can only reach 1,8,8,2,2, and in the bar's palette index 7 is RED and 8 is PINK, 1 near-black and 2 dark green, so the red hairline came out pink and the black line green. Nothing is drawn on 0x5F or 0x60; they are only aimed at - and 仲間配置 and ステータス, whose words belong to menu-status-labels, get their chrome rows aimed there too, so the whole bar's frame is the cartridge's own pixels. WHERE THE ROOM COMES FROM: a plate's chrome row is the same eight pixels in every column, so ONE chrome tile per state (0x5F dimmed, 0x60 lit) is pointed at by every chrome row here - メダロッチ's sixteen, メダロット生産's six and セーブ's six. That frees the sixteen tiles メダロッチ used to spend on chrome and text, which become its two eight-tile words, and it frees 0x03/0x07, the cells セーブ shared with メダロッチ (the two-pixel nick the old spec left in メダロッチ's ッ is gone with them). Nothing is drawn on a tile another screen can reach: every tile repainted here is named only by carousel cells. THE OTHER BUDGET is the bar itself: five entries at most, one separator cell each, 27 cells of bar after the navi badge, so the widths sum to 22. medawatch_layout 'es' spends them 8/4/3/4/3 - メダロッチ takes eight, on map rows 40-41 because the icon blits own columns 10-15 of its old row, and メダロット生産 drops to three to pay for it. Hence 'Medarreloj' (58px of 64) and 'Crea' (24px of 24; 'Crear' is 30px and there is no spare cell to buy it a fourth). 'Save' keeps セーブ at three cells - 'Salva' is 28px, and a fourth cell there would cost メダロッチ one of its eight.

glyph_banks.name: parts-panel-kanji-bank
glyph_banks.notes: The bank the Medarotch parts panel really draws its kanji from: 37 plain 4bpp tiles at 0x4C7628 followed, with no gap, by the plain 1024-entry lookup table at 0x4C7AC8 (format and proof in 'kanji glyph banks', navi/gfx.py). 19 cells are filled - 撃 攻 使 症 状 全 体 力 部 回 数 用 敵 and five more - each 8x16 with the 12-row face two rows down, white (15) over an index-5 rim on transparent 0. The panel's text renderer blits one cell per two-byte kanji code, so a word is translated by repainting the cells its codes point at and comes out exactly as wide as the kanji were: 8px per code, i.e. two stacked lines of two capitals for a two-kanji word, the same four-letter abbreviation shape the parts sheet and the terrain table already use. Patched in place - nothing moves, nothing recompresses. A code is repainted EVERYWHERE these screens draw it, so only words whose kanji never occur in another word are listed. Measured over the parts text pool (0x090000-0x095000, 125 strings): 攻 and 撃 are the pair 攻撃 in all 62 occurrences and 症 and 状 the pair 症状 in all 31, so those two are safe; 全 (全体/全パーツ/全て), 使 (使用/使う), 回 (回数/1回に), 部, 力 and 敵 are not, and stay Japanese. Sínt(oma) is the status-ailment category, the one entry of the effect table at 0x09309D with no string translation (its siblings read Daño / Defe / Tram / Cura / Anul / Camb / Estr / Mov.); Ataq(ue) shows inside the part-effect descriptions that are still Japanese. Where a description IS translated the kanji never render and the plates cost nothing.

glyph_banks.name: asset-table-kanji-bank
glyph_banks.notes: The compressed twin of the same idea, reached from the two asset tables (tiles 0x6462C8 + 0x6FBFC8, table 0x64630C + 0x6FBFE8): 36 tiles, 18 cells, a DIFFERENT subset (it carries 外 停 where the parts panel's bank carries 決 落), so it belongs to another screen of the same family. Nothing on the screens reached so far loads it - poisoning the block at 0x646AC0 with all-ink and walking the Medarotch parts/medal panels and a robottle changed no pixel, and no SWI 11 in those runs names it - so it is patched only to keep the two copies of 攻撃 and 症状 saying the same thing wherever the screen that does load it lives. Recompresses bigger than the original and relocates; pointer_index() finds all four sites. Do not put new_cells words here without seeing the screen: growing a bank changes how much the loader decompresses.
